newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Kuwait sells BP shares in largest block sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Kuwait sells BP shares in largest block sale.

text.p: The world's biggest sale of a single block of shares was completed on Thursday as Kuwait successfully disposed of three percent of shares in oil giant British Petroleum.
On the London Stock Exchange, BP shares fell 25-1/2 pence to 719 after 170 million shares formerly held by the Kuwait Investment Office(KIO) were placed with investors across the globe.
"It's been a huge success," said a spokesman for Goldman Sachs, the U.S. investment bank which handled the 1.22 billion pound ($2 billion) deal.
He said the BP shares had been sold at 716 pence each and added there had been strong demand from both institutional and private investors in the U.S., Europe and the far East.
The KIO, which called the sale a "rebalancing exercise" as its holding became diproportionately big, still holds 6.3 percent of BP shares.
The investment group told Reuters it will remain a "core" investor in BP in the foreseeable future. "We have great confidence in the company and its prospects," said president Yousef Alawadi.
He declined to say what profit KIO had made on the sale.
BP stocks have been among the best performing world oil shares in recent years as the company embarked on a massive cost-cutting programme in the early 1990s.
The efficiency drive was carried out after BP slashed its dividend in 1992 when the company was suffering from a heavy debt burden.
The KIO built up its holding in BP when a sale of the company's stock by the British government coincided with the 1987 stock market crash. BP later bought back part of the holding from the KIO.
Industry analysts were unperturbed by the stake sale, saying it would not have an impact on the company's operations, and they expected the shares to recover quickly.
"The fact somebody sells shares does not change the fundamentals of the company," said Paul Spedding at Kleinwort Benson.
The BP sale is Goldman's third major block deal this year.
In February, it sold $732 million worth of shares in RJR Nabisco Holding Corp for U.S. financier Carl Icahn.
A month earlier, Goldman completed the $900 million sale of Guinness shares for LVMH Moet Hennesy Louis Vuitton.
